what_was_built: A Plans page that a project gets without building one. It mounts the provider's own pricing table element, configured from two Django settings the page reads and passes down as attributes. The component itself reads no settings. It carries the signed-in person's email address so a purchase can be attributed back to the account that made it, because the installed backend matches a provider customer to an application user by email address alone. Where either setting is missing the page states the plans cannot be shown and emits no provider element. Where both are present but the provider's library never loaded, a message already rendered hidden in the markup is revealed by a small static script that checks whether the custom element ever registered. The component can be placed on a project's own page, and either the component or the page template can be replaced by a project supplying its own.
criteria_to_check: All five user stories' acceptance scenarios: is each covered by a test that would FAIL if the behaviour regressed?
specific_questions: The constitution amendment is the highest-consequence text in this diff. Articles XII and XIII previously said a publishable key is never read from Django settings by this package; they now say a COMPONENT never reads it and a page this package ships may. Does the amended text actually hold that line, or does it leave room for a component to read settings?

The hidden could-not-be-loaded message must be present in the markup and hidden, never absent, so that revealing it needs no string from JavaScript (FR-010). Is that actually what the template does, and is the message translatable?
The unavailable state must emit NO provider element at all, not an element plus a message. Check the assertion, not just the template.
pricing_table.js: does it do anything beyond checking whether the custom element registered and revealing the hidden message? It must not interpret an error the provider's own element renders.

The override tests boot a fresh process with a settings module that puts a project application ahead of the package. Do they prove the project's markup actually rendered, or only that a page rendered?

decisions.md D5 records that four component tests build their template context directly rather than through the render helper the rest of the file uses. Read D5, then judge whether that deviation hides anything.
Does any test assert the ABSENCE of something as absence rather than as emptiness — specifically, customer-email omitted rather than emitted empty?
